bibliographic.title: Analysis on water use efficiency of Populus euphratica forest ecosystem in arid area
bibliographic.title_raw_stored: Analysis on water use efficiency of Populus euphratica forest ecosystem in arid area

scope_reason: Drought and high-temperature language appears, but the paper characterises one year of ecosystem carbon/water fluxes and their meteorological covariates; no drought event, heat hazard or impact is examined.

scope_span.evidence_text: explored the main controlling factors of WUE in drought-stressed environment based on the synchronous meteorological data

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: Under the conditions of high temperature, strong radiation and low humidity in the summer, the growth rate of ET was much larger than that of GPP.
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Seasonal covariate relationship within one year of flux data, not a hazard or hazard impact.

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: Moderate drought is beneficial to improve WUE (Krishnan et al. 2006;Yang et al. 2016), but if the drought continues to increase, the intensity of photosynthesis will decrease (Zhao et al. 2007).
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Cited literature used to interpret a soil-water correlation; drought not examined as an event.

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: because long-term drought enhanced the ecosystem's resistance and resilience to water scarcity in order to mitigate the effects of water loss (Gang et al. 2016)
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Cited explanatory statement; not tested by the paper.
